recipes.name: Steak
ingredients: For the New York Strip Steak
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 clove garlic, finely minced or pressed
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 lb chuck steak, trimmed of sinew
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
instructions: For Steak Cuts: Technique:
For the New York Strip Steak
Generously oil a cast iron pan over high heat until absolutely smoking. - neutral oil
Then, sear the steak on both sides hot and fast. - New York Strip Steak
Once a dark crust forms, lower the heat then add butter and garlic. - 4 tbsp butter - 4 cloves garlic whole
Spoon the sizzling butter over the steak, optionally using a sprig of thyme or rosemary to additionally mop the steak down with the butter. - rosemary or thyme sprig optional
Transfer the steak to a plate, pour the hot butter over top, and let rest for 10 minutes.
Before serving, rub the top of the steak with a whole clove of garlic. - garlic whole

Slice and serve with freshly chopped parsley, salt, and freshly ground black pepper. - freshly chopped parsley for garnish - salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste - For the New York Strip Steak
For the Boneless Short Ribs
Salt short ribs and refrigerate uncovered overnight. - boneless short ribs - kosher salt
Set the grill to ‘two-zone’ fire.
Grill over the hot side to sear, then move to the cool side until medium rare. Rest 10 minutes. - 2 lbs boneless short ribs
Toast Hoagie rolls on the grill. - Hoagie rolls
Slice thin against the grain. - For the Boneless Short Ribs
Pile beef on rolls, top with cheese, and broil until melted. - sliced provolone or Muenster cheese - For the Boneless Short Ribs
Simmer beef stock with roux, soy, and Worcestershire into dipping jus. - 2 cups beef stock - 1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp flour (light roux) - 1 tbsp soy sauce - 1 tsp Worcestershire
Serve sandwiches with hot jus on the side. - For the Boneless Short Ribs - For the Hot Jus
For the London Broil

Whisk marinade and pour over steak in a zip bag. Marinate 4–8 hours. - London broil (top round) - ½ cup soy sauce - 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar - 2 tbsp ketchup - 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce - ½ tsp garlic powder - ½ tsp onion powder - 1 tsp paprika - ¼ tsp cayenne - ½ tsp ground sage - ½ tsp salt - 1 tsp black pepper
Pat dry, grill hot and fast to medium rare. Rest 10 minutes. - For the London Broil
Slice very thin across the grain. Serve hot with gravy or chilled as homemade roast beef cold cuts. - For the London Broil
For the Ribeye
Place ribeyes in the smoker at 225°F until internal temp reaches 110–115°F. - bone in ribeyes salted overnight
Rest briefly, then sear over ripping hot cast-iron or grill to develop crust. - For the Ribeye
Slice and serve immediately. - For the Ribeye
For the Hanger Steak
Season hanger steak generously. - hanger steak - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Prepare the grill for ‘two-zone’ fire.
Sear over the hot grill, then move to the cooler side until medium rare. Rest 10 minutes. - For the Hanger Steak
Slice against grain at slight diagonal to avoid overly wide pieces. - For the Hanger Steak
Plate with a mountain of fries. Finish with salt, pepper, and optional butter drizzle. - french fries (homemade or frozen) - salt - black pepper - butter
For Filet Mignon: Steak Tartare:
For the Steak
Trim all fat and connective tissue. - 1 filet mignon
Then, thinly slice into planks, cut the planks into strips, then chop the strips into tiny cubes. - 1 filet mignon
Chop finely to ensure a consistent texture throughout. - 1 filet mignon
For the Dressing

Heat light olive oil in a nonstick sauté pan until shimmering. Add all but 1 tbsp capers, frying until crisp, and draining on paper towels. Reserve oil. - ⅓ cup vegetable oil - ⅓ cup capers drained and dried

In a small bowl, whisk together parsley, remaining capers, shallot, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp reserved fried caper oil, apple cider vinegar, anchovy paste, kosher salt, and freshly ground pepper. - 1 tbsp parsley finely chopped - 1 tsp shallot finely minced - ¼ garlic clove grated - 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce - ½ tsp Dijon mustard - 1 tsp apple cider vinegar - ¼ tsp anchovy paste - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground pepper to taste
For the Serving
Combine dressing and beef - mix thoroughly - For the Dressing - For the Steak
Press the steak tartare into a container forming a puck.
Turn out the formed puck onto a serving plate, then top with a raw egg yolk and garnish with fried capers and a few leaves of parsley. - raw egg yolk - parsley leaves to garnish
Serve immediately with bruschette chips. - bruschette chips
For Sirloin: Beef Stroganoff:
For the Beef
Slice the sirloin thinly into bite-sized pieces then coat and toss with baking soda. - baking soda - 2 lbs sirloin trimmed
Then transfer to the fridge for no more than 45 minutes. - For the Beef
While the beef is marinating, prepare the shallot, - small shallot diced
After 45 minutes have elapsed, rinse the beef thoroughly then pat dry using paper towels. - For the Beef
Add neutral oil to a wok and heat until smoking. Then add the beef, searing and tossing with a wooden spoon. Cook until just brown then remove from the pan. - For the Beef - neutral oil
For the Sauce
Using the same wok over medium-high heat, add shallot and freshly grated garlic. Sauté until fragrant then deglaze with beef stock. - small shallot diced - 1 cup beef stock
In a separate pan, cook shiitake mushrooms over medium heat until brown and fragrant. Then add thyme. - shiitake mushrooms sliced - 1 tsp dried thyme
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the pasta. - 8 oz pasta cooked
Add 1 to 2 tbsp of the reduced stock to the sour cream and mix until homogenous. - sour cream - 1 cup beef stock

Then, add cooked shiitake mushrooms to the wok along with the beef, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir to combine. - shiitake mushrooms sliced - 1 tbsp soy sauce - 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce - For the Beef
Cover with a lid and let the residual heat finish cooking the beef. - For the Beef
Meanwhile, strain the pasta and add butter and salt. - butter to taste - kosher salt to taste - 8 oz pasta cooked
Combine cornstarch in a bowl with 1 tablespoon water or stock - add to the sauce and allow to simmer for 1-2 minutes, or until slightly thickened. - 1 tablespoon corn starch - 1 cup beef stock
For the Assembly
When the beef is finished cooking through, kill the heat. Then add the tempered sour cream, mixing to combine. - Tempered sour cream
Finally, plate the cooked pasta and serve the Beef Stroganoff over top. - 8 oz pasta cooked - For the Beef
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley and freshly ground black pepper. - parsley freshly chopped - freshly ground black pepper to taste
For Skirt Steak: Carne Asada:
For the Marinade
Prepare a large ziptop bag for the marinade by folding down the top.

Add olive oil, soy sauce, lime juice, cumin, dried oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cayenne pepper, freshly ground black pepper, and kosher salt to a mixing bowl. Whisk to combine. - ½ cup extra virgin olive oil - ½ cup soy sauce - 4 tbsp (2) limes juice - 1 tsp cumin - 1 ½ tsp dried oregano - ½ tsp garlic powder - ½ tsp onion powder - 1 ½ tsp paprika - ¼ tsp cayenne pepper - 1 ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper - 2 tsp kosher salt
Then, transfer the marinade to the prepared ziptop bag. - For the Marinade
Add the skirt steak, squeeze out excess air, then massage the bag to ensure every piece is evenly coated. - skirt steak trimmed - For the Marinade
Place the entire bag in a bowl to prevent leakage, then refrigerate for 45 minutes or up to about 3 hours. - For the Marinade - For the Steak
For the Grilling
Prepare for grilling with a ‘two-zone fire’.
If using a (gas grill), turn the burners on one side of the grill all the way up to high and the other side low or even off.
If using a (charcoal grill), pile all the charcoal on one side of the grill.

Once the steak is done marinating, sear the steak on both sides on the hot side of the grill, then transfer to the cool side of the grill, cover, and finish cooking to desired doneness. - marinated steak
If you’re using the steak to make a burrito, prep any burrito toppings during this time.
For the Serving
Sliced the grilled steak (across the grain) into thin slices and serve hot. - For the Steak
For the Burrito Assembly
Alternatively, cut the grilled steak into bite-sized pieces and serve in a burrito. - For the Steak

Wrap all of your burrito toppings and steak in the grilled tortilla, then wrap tightly with aluminum foil. Optionally return to the grill for 5 minutes covered for final serving. - grilled tortillas - roasted red peppers and poblanos - shredded cheese - cooked Mexican rice - For the Steak
For Delmonico Steak: Cheesesteak:
For the Steak
Place whole steaks on a sheet of parchment paper then transfer to the freezer for 30 to 40 minutes depending on the power of your freezer. - ribeye steaks
The steaks should be very firm but not frozen all the way through, but the first centimeter or two should be almost frozen. - For the Steak
Once firm, slice the steaks very very thinly. - For the Steak
Heat fat in a sauté pan until shimmering, then add the shaved steak. - fat or oil - ribeye steaks
Sear until nice and brown on one side. Then, flip, searing until brown on the other side. - For the Steak
For the Assembly

Arrange the seared steak into a sandwich-like shape in the pan then drape with cheese slices. Turn down the heat, add a splash of water, and cover until the cheese is melted. - seared steak - sliced cheese of your choosing - splash of water
Prepare a hoagie roll with mayo, then transfer the melted cheese and steak to the roll. Serve hot and enjoy! - hoagie roll - mayo to taste - seared steak
For Chuck Steak: Steak Hachė:
Place the blade of your food processor in the freezer for 30 minutes.
Cube chuck steak, freeze for 20 minutes until firm. - 1 lb chuck steak trimmed of sinew
Then pulse in the food processor with the chilled blade into coarse grind. - 1 lb chuck steak trimmed of sinew
Form thick oval patties (~8 oz each). Season with salt. - 1 lb chuck steak trimmed of sinew - kosher salt to taste
Grill or sear until medium rare. Rest briefly.
Plate simply with mustard, parsley, and pepper. Eat with a fork and knife like a steak. - grain mustard for serving - parsley for serving - freshly ground black pepper to taste
For Steak Pinwheels:
Butterfly flank steak and pound to even thickness. Season with salt. - 2 lbs flank steak butterflied - kosher salt to taste
Preheat oven to 375 °F.

Layer cheese and vegetables, leaving 1-inch border on the bottom of the steak. Roll tightly into a log. - 10 slices cheese (mozzarella or Muenster) - 1 cup sautéed peppers and onions - 2 lbs flank steak butterflied
Tie with twine every 2 inches, then slice into pinwheels.
Sear on a hot grill or skillet to seal in cheese, then finish in the oven until medium.
Rest briefly, slice cleanly, and serve cheesy steak spirals.
